```python
import tensorflow as tf

# The original bug report involves a crash in PyTorch's Inductor compiler 
# when handling int64 tensors generated by iota (arange) followed by a max operation.
# This test case adapts the core logic to TensorFlow, using tf.keras.backend.name_scope
# to structure the graph operations, and tf.function to mimic the compilation aspect of torch.compile.

@tf.function
def test_int64_arange_max():
    with tf.keras.backend.name_scope("int64_arange_max_scope"):
        # Corresponds to: torch.ops.prims.iota.default(36, start = 0, step = 1, dtype = torch.int64, ...)
        # In TensorFlow, tf.range is the equivalent operation.
        iota = tf.range(0, 36, dtype=tf.int64)

        # Corresponds to: torch.ops.aten.view.default(iota, [1, 36])
        # In TensorFlow, tf.reshape is the equivalent operation.
        view_3 = tf.reshape(iota, [1, 36])

        # Corresponds to: torch.ops.aten.max.default(view_3)
        # In TensorFlow, tf.reduce_max computes the max of elements across dimensions of a tensor.
        max_1 = tf.reduce_max(view_3)

        return max_1

# Execute the compiled function
result = test_int64_arange_max()

# Verify the result. 
# The range is 0 to 35, so the max value should be 35.
expected_value = 35
assert result == expected_value, f"Expected max value to be {expected_value}, but got {result}"

print("Test passed. The logic executed successfully within tf.keras.backend.name_scope.")
```
